deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page (18r) worked with the four-point Euler integral ∫Z dz, Z=(z-a)^α(z-b)^β(z-c)^γ(z-d)^δ. There α+β+γ+δ=-2, so that ∞ is not a singular point. It introduced Riemann's integral-normalised function
  𝔓(α,β,γ,x) = ∫_0^1 y^α (1-y)^β (1-xy)^γ dy
and derived three-term relations from the closed-contour (half-plane) argument. One of them is
  𝔓(α,δ,γ,1-x) sin(γ+δ)π = -x^{γ+δ+1} 𝔓(δ,γ,β,x) sin γπ + 𝔓(α,β,γ,x) sin βπ.
It also rewrote these relations in exponent-difference notation P(λ,μ,ν,x). (The transcription uses Γ for this function; on the page it is the same fraktur 𝔓.)

TOP OF PAGE.
- The first line finishes the sentence from 18r: '...wenn man μ und ν das entgegengesetzte Zeichen gibt.' The remaining relations follow by changing the signs of μ and ν.
- The sketch shows circles of convergence about 0 and 1 on the real axis, with labels x/(1-x) and ∞. Riemann is visualising where the expansions in x, 1-x and x/(x-1) converge.
- A crossed-out 'a+0i, a-0i' (top right) recalls the boundary values above and below the cut.

'INTEGRALE' PARAGRAPH (modern restatement).
- Exponent-difference reading. Read P(λ,μ,ν,x) with λ the exponent difference at 0. Matching 18r (λ=α+β+1, μ=α+γ+1, ν=α+δ+1=-(β+γ+1)), μ belongs to ∞ and ν to 1.
- Claim: a given branch at 0 can be written in 8 ways, itself plus 7 others:
  - P(λ,±μ,±ν,x): the identity, the a↔b swap and the Euler transformation (1-x)^{c-a-b}F(c-a,c-b;c;x);
  - P(λ,±ν,±μ,x/(x-1)): the Pfaff transformations, which swap the points 1 and ∞.
- Riemann then notes that P(λ,-μ,ν,x) and P(λ,μ,ν,x) give the same series. So do P(λ,μ,-ν,x) and P(λ,-μ,-ν,x). Changing the sign of the ∞-difference only swaps a and b.
- Hence each member of an equation can be expanded in only 2 genuinely different power series in x. The two series in x/(x-1) converge only while Re x < 1/2 (|x/(x-1)|<1 ⇔ Re x<1/2).
- Between the series in x/(x-1) and in (x-1)/x, an equation can hold only on the circle of modulus 1. Elsewhere one series diverges where the other converges, so such an equation holds only for the integrals, i.e. the analytic continuations.

FORMULAS.
(1) Series expansion of the integral. Expand (1-xy)^γ = Σ Π(n-1-γ)/(Π(-1-γ)Πn) x^n y^n and integrate termwise with ∫_0^1 y^{n+α}(1-y)^β dy = Π(n+α)Πβ/Π(n+α+β+1). This gives
  𝔓(α,β,γ,x) = [Πβ/Π(-1-γ)] Σ_n Π(n-1-γ)Π(n+α)/(Πn Π(n+α+β+1)) x^n.
  Correct. In modern terms 𝔓 = B(α+1,β+1)·₂F₁(-γ,α+1;α+β+2;x). The trailing 'sin γπ/(-sin γπ)' fragment is a stray note.
(2) The same with (α,β,γ)→(δ,γ,β), times x^{δ+γ+1}:
  x^{δ+γ+1} 𝔓(δ,γ,β,x) = [Πγ/Π(-1-β)] Σ Π(n-1-β)Π(n+δ)/(Πn Π(n+δ+γ+1)) x^{n+γ+δ+1}.
  On the left Riemann writes 𝔓(α,δ,γ,1-x) sin(γ+δ)π = ..., i.e. he is about to substitute into the 18r relation.
(3) Substitution [my filled step]. Πβ sin βπ = π/Π(-1-β) and Πγ sin γπ = π/Π(-1-γ) (reflection formula). Then
  𝔓(α,δ,γ,1-x) sin(γ+δ)π · Π(-1-β)Π(-1-γ)/π = S1 - S2,
  where S1 = Σ Π(n-1-γ)Π(n+α)/(ΠnΠ(n+α+β+1)) x^n and S2 = Σ Π(n-1-β)Π(n+δ)/(ΠnΠ(n+δ+γ+1)) x^{n+γ+δ+1}.
  Riemann writes the left side with sin(α+β)π/π. The margin notes 'α+β+γ+δ' and 'dα=-dδ' record that the parameter sum is fixed.
(4) Degenerate (logarithmic) case. He sets γ+δ+1 = -m with m a positive integer; the exponent x^{n-m} in the last line fixes the sign. Then sin(α+β)π→0 and 1/Π(n+γ+δ+1)→0 for n<m. He uses the reflection formula Π(n+δ+γ+1)Π(-n-δ-γ-2) = (-1)^n π/sin(δ+γ)π to pass to the limit. The finite principal part comes out as
  𝔓(α,δ,γ,1-x) Π(-1-γ)Π(-1-β) = Σ_{n=0}^{m-1} (-1)^n Π(n-1-β)Π(n+δ)Π(m-n-1)/Πn · x^{n-m} + [the remaining terms].
  The remaining terms are the logarithmic series. The next page carries this out with ψ-functions and log z (in a confluent limit).
Purpose: the connection problem for the hypergeometric/P-function between the singular points 0 and 1, including the degenerate integer-exponent case.
errors: Sign slip in formula (3), assuming the reading is right. With α+β+γ+δ=-2, sin(γ+δ)π = -sin(α+β)π. The correct identity is 𝔓(α,δ,γ,1-x)·sin(α+β)π·Π(-1-γ)Π(-1-β)/π = -S1 + S2, not S1 - S2. Equivalently, the 18r relation reads 𝔓(α,δ,γ,1-x) sin(α+β)π = -sin βπ 𝔓(α,β,γ,x) + sin γπ x^{γ+δ+1}𝔓(δ,γ,β,x). I checked this against the standard ₂F₁ connection formula.

This sign propagates into the final line. In the limit γ+δ+1→-m, the correct coefficient of x^{n-m} is -(-1)^n Π(n-1-β)Π(n+δ)Π(m-n-1)/Πn, not +(-1)^n. The final line is consistent with Riemann's own (slipped) line (3).

The reflection step is written incompletely ('Π(n+δ+γ+1)Π(...-n) = π/sin(δ+γ..)π'). The exact form is Π(n+δ+γ+1)Π(-n-δ-γ-2) = (-1)^n π/sin((δ+γ)π). The (-1)^n factor is not visible in the written line.
The convergence remark 'Re x < 1/2' is correct for the x/(x-1) series. The remark about the series in x/(x-1) versus (x-1)/x holding only on the unit circle is heuristic but correct in spirit.

results.what: A branch of the P-function at 0 has 8 representations: P(λ,±μ,±ν,x) and P(λ,±ν,±μ,x/(x-1)). These pair into identical series, so there are only 2 distinct power series in x.
results.modern_name: Kummer's solutions (Euler and Pfaff transformations) restricted to the stabiliser of the point 0
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (1778), Pfaff (1797), Kummer (1836); P-function form by Riemann (1857)

results.what: The series in x/(x-1) converge exactly for Re x < 1/2. Equations between series in reciprocal variables can hold only on the unit circle, otherwise only between the analytic continuations.
results.modern_name: Domain of convergence of Pfaff-transformed series; analytic continuation

results.what: Termwise expansion of ∫_0^1 y^α(1-y)^β(1-xy)^γ dy as a hypergeometric series.
Connection formula expressing 𝔓(α,δ,γ,1-x) through the two branches at 0, rewritten via the reflection formula as a difference of two power series.
results.modern_name: Gauss–Kummer connection formula for ₂F₁ between z=1 and z=0

results.what: Limit when the exponent difference at 0 is an integer (γ+δ+1=-m). A finite Laurent part with Π(m-n-1) coefficients appears; logarithmic terms follow (on the next page).
results.modern_name: Logarithmic (degenerate) case of the hypergeometric connection formula

deep.surprise_reason: Everything here is the standard material of Kummer's 24 solutions, the Euler integral and the Gauss–Kummer connection formula, in the form Riemann published in 1857. The degenerate-case computation is routine working-out with a sign slip. These are working notes toward the 1857 paper, not new results.

transcription_corrections: First line: 'gesetzte Zeichen gibt.' It completes '...das entgegengesetzte Zeichen gibt' from the previous page.
The function symbol written 'Γ(α,β,γ,x)' in the formulas is Riemann's fraktur 𝔓 (same as P on 18r), not Gamma.
'P(λ-μ,ν,x) und P(λ,μ,ν,x) geben gleiche Reihen' should read 'P(λ,-μ,ν,x) und P(λ,μ,ν,x) geben gleiche Reihen'.
'jedes Glied der Gleichung nur ∂/· gewisse Reihe' is most likely '...nur [in] 2 gewisse Reihen nach Potenzen von x [entwickeln]'.
'Die beiden Reihen x/(x-1) convergiren nur so lange der reelle Theil von x < 1/2' (an inserted 'von x' above the line).
Second formula line: the left side is 𝔓(α,δ,γ,1-x)·sin(γ+δ)π = ..., with x^{δ+γ+1}𝔓(δ,γ,β,x) written above as a note.
'γ+δ+1 = [-m-]' should be 'γ+δ+1 = -m' (crossed/overwritten). This is consistent with x^{n-m} in the last line.
'dα = [-d-]δ' should be 'dα = -dδ' (the parameter sum α+β+γ+δ is held fixed).
The summation limits in the last line are n = 0,...,m-1, followed by '+' (continuation with the logarithmic terms).
